title: feat: Convert filters to ObjectStack FilterNode AST format
body:
## ✅ ObjectStack Filter Rules Update - Complete

### Summary
Successfully updated all filter handling code to comply with **ObjectStack Protocol v0.1.2+** filter rules. All filters are now converted to **FilterNode AST format** for compatibility with the latest ObjectStack specification.

### Changes Made
- [x] Understand current filter usage in codebase
- [x] Update objectstack-adapter.ts to handle new filter rules
- [x] Update ObjectQLDataSource.ts to handle new filter rules  
- [x] Add tests for filter conversion to AST format
- [x] Review and update filter-related documentation
- [x] Test with full test suite (119 tests passing ✅)
- [x] Address code review feedback
  - [x] Extract filter conversion to shared utility (eliminates code duplication)
  - [x] Add warning for $regex operator (semantic clarity)
  - [x] Throw error for unknown operators (no silent failures)
  - [x] Add FilterNode type definition (better type safety)
  - [x] Add comprehensive tests (12 new tests)
- [x] Run security scan (0 vulnerabilities ✅)
- [x] Verify no breaking changes introduced (backward compatible ✅)

### Filter Conversion Details
**Simple filters:** `{ status: 'active' }` → `['status', '=', 'active']`  
**Complex filters:** `{ age: { $gte: 18, $lte: 65 } }` → `['and', ['age', '>=', 18], ['age', '<=', 65]]`

**Supported operators:** $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin/$notin, $contains, $startswith, $between

### Code Review Improvements
✅ **No code duplication** - Filter conversion logic extracted to shared utility  
✅ **$regex warning** - Users warned about limited regex support  
✅ **Unknown operator errors** - No silent failures on unrecognized operators  
✅ **Better types** - FilterNode type definition for improved type safety

### Test Results
- **119 tests passing** (12 new filter converter tests added)
- **0 security vulnerabilities** (CodeQL scan clean)
- **All builds successful**
